COVID-19: Changes to biometrics requirement for in-Canada temporary residence applicants
As a temporary measure, if you’re in Canada and applying to work, study or stay temporarily in Canada, you do not need to give your biometrics. Learn more about the exemption .

context.title: Dual Canadian citizens need a valid Canadian passport
context.text:
Canadian-American dual citizens
To fly to Canada, you need
- either your valid U.S. passport or your valid Canadian passport
- to meet the basic requirements to enter Canada
If you travel with just your valid U.S. passport, you
- will need to carry identification that shows your Canadian citizenship
- may be asked to go through immigration screening
Even though you only need one of your passports to enter Canada, you should travel with both . Having both passports makes travel between Canada and the United States easier. Your passports prove
- your citizenships
- that you have the right to enter Canada and the U.S. without immigration screening

context.title: Dual Canadian citizens need a valid Canadian passport
context.text:
Find out if you are eligible for a special authorization to board your flight to Canada
You can apply for a special authorization if you:
- have not been issued a Canadian passport that is valid on the day of your travel
- have a flight to Canada that leaves in less than 10 days
- have a valid passport from a visa-exempt country or territory
- are not a Canadian-American dual citizen
And one of the following:
- have previously received a certificate of Canadian citizenship, or
- held a Canadian passport in the past, or
- were granted Canadian citizenship after having been a permanent resident of Canada.
Your information will be verified in our electronic systems to confirm that you are a Canadian citizen. This authorization will be valid for only 4 days from the date of travel you select on the form . If you don’t use it within this time, you will need to apply for a new authorization.

context.title: Dual Canadian citizens need a valid Canadian passport
context.text:
Dual citizens returning to Canada
When boarding your flight, you must show
- a printed or electronic copy of your Special Authorization approval email
- a proof of Canadian citizenship (including a citizenship certificate, or provincial or territorial birth certificate), if available
Without these documents, you may be denied boarding.
Continue to special authorization request .
If you are not eligible for the special authorization
There are no quick fixes to help you get on your flight.
Contact the nearest Government of Canada office abroad to find out what your options are . Only under strict conditions and on a case-by-case basis will temporary passports or emergency travel documents be issued.
Need help? Find answers to your questions about the Canadian passport .

context.title: Study permit: How to apply
context.text:

If you’re applying for a study permit, you must apply online , whether you’re outside of Canada or already in Canada.
You’re only eligible to apply on paper if you
- have a disability that prevents you from applying online
- hold an identity or travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons
Get faster processing as a doctoral student New
If you’re a doctoral (PhD) student, you and your accompanying family members may be able to get faster processing on your applications.
Check if you’re eligible and learn how to get your applications processed faster.

context.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
context.text:
Option 1 (recommended): Reply to your invitation
Reply to the office that sent you the invitation.
Option 2: Send us a web form
You can also request an accommodation by sending us a web form .
If you need a waiver (exemption)
If you have a situation that prevents you from meeting a requirement, you can request a waiver instead of an accommodation. You can request a waiver for these requirements:
- Citizenship test and language requirement: Your situation must meet the waiver criteria .
- Oath of citizenship : We’ll only give a waiver if a mental disability (like an intellectual or a developmental disability) prevents an applicant from understanding the oath.
- For example, they don’t understand that taking the oath makes them a Canadian citizen.
If we approve your waiver request, you don’t need to meet the requirement (for example, you don’t need to take the test).
Learn more about the waiver

context.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements: after you submit your request
context.text:
If we refuse your waiver request
We’ll send you a letter to let you know if we refuse a request.
You must take the test, prove your language skills or take the oath (depending on the waiver you asked for).
If you need help meeting these requirements, you can request an accommodation for accessibility or another reason .

context.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements: after you submit your request
context.text:
After you submit your waiver request
After we get your request, we’ll
- review it to make sure that you qualify for the waiver
- tell you our decision or ask for more information
We can’t guarantee the approval of a waiver request. Our officers will review all requests on a case-by-case basis.
If we approve your waiver request
You do not need to take the test, prove your language skills or take the oath of citizenship (depending on the waiver of you asked for).
If you check your application status , these sections of the status tracker will have a “ Waived ” status (where applicable):
- Citizenship test
- Language skills
- Citizenship ceremony

context.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements
context.text:
Waiver for citizenship requirements
To become a Canadian citizen, you must meet certain requirements when you apply. If you can’t meet a specific requirement, you can request an exemption. This is called a waiver. If your waiver is approved, it means you don’t need to meet that requirement.
You can only request a waiver for
- the citizenship test
- proving your English or French language skills
- the oath of citizenship
If you can meet the requirement but you need help with it , request an accommodation instead .

context.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements
context.text:
Accommodation
Examples of an accommodation are:
- other accessible versions of the test, such as Braille, large-print, or oral tests
- extra time to take the test for someone with a disability
- sign language interpretation and wheelchair access at citizenship events (like a ceremony or an interview)
Learn more about accommodations (opens in a new tab)
For more information
Learn about all the requirements to become a Canadian citizen .

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
context.text:
How to host a ceremony
Explore the steps, guidelines and best practices that will help you host a memorable citizenship ceremony.
Steps to host a ceremony
- Contact us What to include in your request
Contact us
If you’re interested in hosting a citizenship ceremony, submit your hosting request by
- email , or
- mail to your closest Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) office
To avoid delays, send your request only once .
What to include in your request
- Use the subject line in your email or letter: “Citizenship Ceremony Hosting Request – [Proposed date]”
- Tell us in English or French :
- name of your organization
- brief description of your organization
- contact person’s name, telephone and email
- type of citizenship ceremony you’d like to host (in-person or virtual)
- proposed dates for the ceremony
- for an in-person ceremony , also include:
- proposed venue
- room capacity (ideally large enough to accommodate candidates and their guests)

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Who can host a ceremony
context.text:
Who can host a ceremony
We encourage collaborations with a wide variety of groups and organizations to make citizenship ceremonies open and welcoming to the general public.
Your organization can work with us as the “host” of the ceremony.
Eligible hosts
Groups or organizations that can host a ceremony include:
- non-governmental and non-profit organizations
- educational institutions
- service organizations
- veterans’ organizations
- libraries
- volunteer groups
- various community groups
- government organizations or departments at all levels (federal, provincial/territorial, municipal)
- for example, City of Montréal, Province of Manitoba, provincial courts, Parks Canada

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
context.text:
Don't
- share personal, political, religious or controversial points of view
- promote, advertise or sell any product, service or business
- ask a host representative or other individual to preside over the ceremony
- assign a presiding official such as a citizenship judge or volunteer presiding official – only IRCC officials can assign presiding officials
- organize a ceremony that’s exclusive to candidates of a specific ethnic, religious, gender or age group
- create or distribute a “congratulatory certificate” – this may be mistaken for the official Canadian citizenship certificate
- produce or share any ceremony-related materials or instructions for special guests without IRCC approval

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: When and where to host a ceremony
context.text:
Where to host a ceremony
Ceremony venues depend on whether the event is virtual or in-person.
Virtual ceremony
- Hosted using videoconferencing software.
- IRCC staff will set up the virtual ceremony.
In-person ceremony
Hosts must consult with IRCC staff to confirm the venue.
In-person citizenship ceremonies can be held at:
- your local IRCC office
- a community venue that’s accessible and appropriate for the occasion
Keep in mind that family and friends often attend this special occasion and larger venues are often preferred.

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
context.text:
- proposed dates for the ceremony
- for an in-person ceremony , also include:
- proposed venue
- room capacity (ideally large enough to accommodate candidates and their guests)
- accessibility details, such as
- washrooms
- accessible parking
- wheelchair access
- mobility aids
- seating areas
- an alternate venue if ceremony is planned outside (in case of rain)
- Work with us to plan the ceremony

context.title: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: How to apply
context.text:
If you’re getting help with your application from someone else
You can ask someone to help you with your immigration application.

If you’re using a paid immigration representative
Paid immigration representatives need to be authorized (opens in a new tab) .

- download the Use of a Representative (IMM 5476) form
- complete and sign it
- get your representative to sign it
- upload it with your application

QUESTION: How do I request to host a citizenship ceremony?

question: How do I request to host a citizenship ceremony?

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Who can host a ceremony
context.text:
Who can host a ceremony
We encourage collaborations with a wide variety of groups and organizations to make citizenship ceremonies open and welcoming to the general public.
Your organization can work with us as the “host” of the ceremony.
Eligible hosts
Groups or organizations that can host a ceremony include:
- non-governmental and non-profit organizations
- educational institutions
- service organizations
- veterans’ organizations
- libraries
- volunteer groups
- various community groups
- government organizations or departments at all levels (federal, provincial/territorial, municipal)
- for example, City of Montréal, Province of Manitoba, provincial courts, Parks Canada

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: When and where to host a ceremony
context.text:
Where to host a ceremony
Ceremony venues depend on whether the event is virtual or in-person.
Virtual ceremony
- Hosted using videoconferencing software.
- IRCC staff will set up the virtual ceremony.
In-person ceremony
Hosts must consult with IRCC staff to confirm the venue.
In-person citizenship ceremonies can be held at:
- your local IRCC office
- a community venue that’s accessible and appropriate for the occasion
Keep in mind that family and friends often attend this special occasion and larger venues are often preferred.

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Guidelines and resources
context.text:
Social media guidelines
If you’re sharing information about a citizenship ceremony on social media, before or after the event, follow these guidelines:
Hosts
- Clearly identify your role using phrases such as
- “Host of an Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada citizenship ceremony”
- “An Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada citizenship ceremony hosted by [host name] will take place on [date].”
- Post in both English and French.
- Don’t include the names, photos or images of the presiding official or special guests.
- IRCC will thank the host during the ceremony and may mention them in media advisories, if applicable.

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Guidelines and resources
context.text:
Guidelines for posters and materials
If you create a poster or other material to highlight the event, follow these rules.
What your posters or materials must include
Posters and materials must
- be in both English and French, even if the ceremony is mostly in 1 language
- be neutral, non-partisan and non-religious
- focus on the citizenship ceremony only ( don’t highlight other activities or programs of the host organization or the sponsors)
- clearly state the host using phrases such as
- “[host name], Host of an Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada citizenship ceremony”
- “An Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada citizenship ceremony, hosted by [host name], will take place on [date]”
- use only photos you have permission to use (you own or purchased them)
- show the ceremony start time, not the registration time
- be submitted to IRCC for review and approval
- display materials in community spaces before the ceremony

context.title: Citizenship ceremony: Ceremony formats
context.text:
Ceremony formats
If we invite you to the ceremony, you’ll attend
- a virtual ceremony or
- an in-person ceremony
Virtual ceremony
We may invite you to attend a virtual ceremony by video conference.
Check your ceremony invitation for the date, time and video conference link.
Here’s what a virtual ceremony is like:
The virtual Canadian citizenship ceremony
This video will help you learn what to expect on the day of the virtual ceremony.
This video is also available in high definition (HD) on YouTube . You can share it on your social media channels or embed it on your website.
Transcript

question: Do I need to fill out the Residence Outside of Canada form (CIT 0177) for my child who lived abroad with me as a family member of a Crown servant during the eligibility period for Canadian citizenship?

context.title: Canadian citizenship for minor 5(1) : Forms and documents to apply on paper
context.text:
Residence outside Canada with a Crown servant (Cit 0177)
If the minor spent time outside Canada as a family member of a Crown servant during their eligibility period, download and complete the Residence Outside of Canada form (CIT 0177) (opens in a new tab) .
The eligibility period is 5 years before the date the application is signed.
- It covers the time when the minor has been a permanent resident (PR).
- If the minor has been a PR for less than 5 years, the eligibility period includes the entire time they’ve held the PR status.
A Crown servant
- is a person employed in or with the Canadian Armed Forces, the federal public administration or the public service of a province or territory
- doesn’t include locally engaged employees (foreign citizens hired in their own countries by the Canadian government to support Canadian offices abroad)
A family member of a Crown servant includes their
- child
- spouse
- common law partner

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
context.text:
If you’re applying for yourself
You can apply online if you were born on or after February 15, 1977, and you
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or after April 17, 2009, or
- were born outside of Canada to a parent who was:
- born in Canada on or after February 15, 1977, or
- granted Canadian citizenship on or after April 17, 2009
If you’re a parent applying on behalf of a child (under 18 years old)
You can apply if:
- your child was granted Canadian citizenship on or after April 17, 2009, or
- one of your child's parents was
- born in Canada on or after February 15, 1977, or
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or after April 17, 2009
If you’re applying for your child(ren):
- you can only submit applications for 3 children at the same time
- you must be the child’s biological parent or legal parent at birth
- the reason for applying must be the same for everyone (for example, all of your children need to replace their lost certificates)

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
context.text:
If you need urgent processing
We may be able to process your application faster in some cases.
You need to apply on paper
You need to apply on paper if
- you were born in Canada on or before February 14, 1977
- you became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or before April 16, 2009
- you were born outside of Canada to a parent who
- was born in Canada on or before February 16, 1977, or
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or before April 16, 2009
- you’re applying for minors (under 18) for whom you’re the legal guardian
- you or a minor was born in Canada
- you need to replace or update your certificate
- you’re applying for 2 to 3 children and only some of them are naturalized Canadian citizens
- you’re applying for 4 or more children
- you’re applying for a replacement certificate for yourself and your children
- you don’t know information about your parents or grandparents
- For example, you don’t know when your parent was born or if your grandparent was a crown servant.

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
context.text:
If you were born and adopted outside Canada
If you were born outside Canada and adopted by a Canadian parent, you’re not automatically a Canadian citizen.
Before submitting an application, learn about citizenship by descent for adopted people .
Minors who are permanent residents
If your minor child is a permanent resident, you will likely need to apply for your child’s Canadian citizenship (naturalization or grant of citizenship) to get a citizenship certificate.
If you apply to become a Canadian citizen
If you apply for and receive Canadian citizenship ( naturalization or grant of citizenship ), you
- will receive the certificate at a citizenship ceremony
- do not need to apply for a citizenship certificate

context.title: Open work permits for family members of work permit holders: How to apply
context.text:
In-Canada applicants
Make sure your eligible family member answers the following questions correctly when they apply.
When your family member is asked the question: “ What is your current immigration status in Canada? ” they must select the answer shown below that applies to their situation:
If your family member’s situation is…
Then the immigration status they should select is…
Working without a work permit
Visitor
Student
Worker
Work permit holder
Worker
Other types of visitors
Visitor
Students must make sure that the rest of their answers on the work permit application form are true and accurate .
- Answer “ Yes ” to the question Are you
- a spouse, common-law partner or dependent child of a foreign worker who holds a valid work permit or is approved for a work permit. Not all family members of workers are eligible. Check if you are eligible to apply for an open work permit ;
- a person who holds a temporary resident permit that is valid for 6 months or more;

context.title: Sponsor your spouse, partner or children: Who you can sponsor
context.text:
If you want to sponsor a child through an intercountry adoption, or an orphaned family member
Follow the steps for
- sponsoring a child through an intercountry adoption , or
- sponsoring an orphaned family member
If you’re only sponsoring your child
Things to know if you’re only sponsoring your child (without sponsoring your spouse or partner):
- If you’re only sponsoring your child, you’ll put your child as the principal applicant in the application. You’ll have to show that the other parent or legal guardian agrees to your child immigrating to Canada. See your document checklist for the documents you’ll need to provide.
- If your child has a child of their own (your grandchild), you must declare your grandchild as a dependant in the application, whether they are coming to Canada or not.

context.title: Minor children travelling to Canada
context.text:
Minor children entering Canada as a visitor
The documents a minor child needs to enter Canada depend on whether the child is travelling alone or with someone.
If a minor child is travelling alone
The child should present
- their own passport
- A parent’s passport, even if the child’s details are included in it, cannot be used.
- a copy of their birth certificate, and
- a letter of authorization, in English or French if possible, which is signed by both parents or by their legal guardian and includes
- the parents’ (or legal guardian’s) address and telephone number, and
- the name, address and telephone number of the adult who will look after the child in Canada

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
context.text:
If you’re applying for yourself
You can apply online if you were born on or after February 15, 1977, and you
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or after April 17, 2009, or
- were born outside of Canada to a parent who was:
- born in Canada on or after February 15, 1977, or
- granted Canadian citizenship on or after April 17, 2009
If you’re a parent applying on behalf of a child (under 18 years old)
You can apply if:
- your child was granted Canadian citizenship on or after April 17, 2009, or
- one of your child's parents was
- born in Canada on or after February 15, 1977, or
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or after April 17, 2009
If you’re applying for your child(ren):
- you can only submit applications for 3 children at the same time
- you must be the child’s biological parent or legal parent at birth
- the reason for applying must be the same for everyone (for example, all of your children need to replace their lost certificates)

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
context.text:
If you need urgent processing
We may be able to process your application faster in some cases.
You need to apply on paper
You need to apply on paper if
- you were born in Canada on or before February 14, 1977
- you became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or before April 16, 2009
- you were born outside of Canada to a parent who
- was born in Canada on or before February 16, 1977, or
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or before April 16, 2009
- you’re applying for minors (under 18) for whom you’re the legal guardian
- you or a minor was born in Canada
- you need to replace or update your certificate
- you’re applying for 2 to 3 children and only some of them are naturalized Canadian citizens
- you’re applying for 4 or more children
- you’re applying for a replacement certificate for yourself and your children
- you don’t know information about your parents or grandparents
- For example, you don’t know when your parent was born or if your grandparent was a crown servant.

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
context.text:
If you were born and adopted outside Canada
If you were born outside Canada and adopted by a Canadian parent, you’re not automatically a Canadian citizen.
Before submitting an application, learn about citizenship by descent for adopted people .
Minors who are permanent residents
If your minor child is a permanent resident, you will likely need to apply for your child’s Canadian citizenship (naturalization or grant of citizenship) to get a citizenship certificate.
If you apply to become a Canadian citizen
If you apply for and receive Canadian citizenship ( naturalization or grant of citizenship ), you
- will receive the certificate at a citizenship ceremony
- do not need to apply for a citizenship certificate

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
context.text:
If you were born in Canada
A provincial or territorial birth certificate should be enough to prove Canadian citizenship.
You may still apply for a citizenship certificate .
If you were born outside Canada to a Canadian parent
You may be a Canadian citizen if your parent was a Canadian citizen when you were born. Some limits apply.
Check if you may be a Canadian citizen. If you want to find out for sure , apply for a citizenship certificate.
If you were born outside Canada on or after December 15, 2025 , and your Canadian parent was born outside Canada, you must prove that your Canadian parent spent 1,095 days in Canada before you were born.
Calculate your parent’s physical presence .

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
context.text:
What we accept
You must include proof of parentage and Canadian citizenship for your Canadian parent, grandparent and parental ancestor as applicable. For each person, you must provide 1 or more of the following documents issued by the original authority:
provincial or territorial birth certificate
If you’re missing any birth certificates
If you don’t have a birth certificate or birth record for yourself or for any of your parental ancestors, you must send other documents to show parentage and Canadian citizenship. These must be issued by the original authority and can include:
- hospital record of birth
- record from a physician or midwife who witnessed the birth
- baptismal certificate or record (including copies or certified records)
- The baptism must have taken place within a reasonable time after the birth.
- census records
- boat manifest
- birth certificate from another country that shows the parent-child relationship in each generation

context.title: Hire skilled youth through International Experience Canada
context.text:
When to submit an offer of employment
You should submit your offer of employment once your candidate receives an ITA. Once they accept the ITA, they’ll have 20 days to submit their complete work permit application.
After you submit your offer of employment
After you submit your offer of employment, give the candidate the offer of employment number, the signed job offer and proof that you paid the employer compliance fee. Then they can submit their work permit application.
The standard processing time for an IEC work permit is 56 days from the time we receive a complete application (including biometric information). If the candidate is approved for a work permit, they can come to Canada to activate their work permit and start working for you on the date specified on their job offer letter.

context.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
context.text:
If you applied as a family or a group with 1 email address
To download the individual e-certificates, provide the following information for each person on the “Download Citizenship e-Certificate” page of the IRCC Portal:
- application number (opens in a new tab) .
- unique client identifier (UCI) (opens in a new tab) .
- date of birth
You don’t have the download instructions letter
We send the letter to the last email address you gave us . This may be the one that
- you put on your online application or paper application form
- you provided after you applied (for example, by using our web form to update your information)
You should
- check for a message from an email address ending in “@cic.gc.ca”
- check your spam or junk folder
If you still can’t find the instructions letter
- you can request a new code
- you need to use a different email from the one you applied with

context.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
context.text:
How to get an e-certificate
The e-certificate is available when you apply:
- to become a Canadian citizen (citizenship grant)
- for a citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship)
- to resume your Canadian citizenship after giving it up
Exceptions for some citizenship applications
If you apply as a stateless person born to a Canadian parent , the certificate is available in paper format only at this time.
We’re working to make sure the e-certificate is available to all successful citizenship applicants in the future.

context.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
context.text:
What you can do with an e-certificate
You can view and download your e-certificate as many times as you want. After downloading an e-certificate, you can
- save it to any device (desktop, laptop, tablet or mobile phone)
- print it as many times you want
- use it to apply for various services and benefits
Valid formats of the e-certificate
The e-certificate is always a valid proof of citizenship even when you
- print it
- display it on your device
- send it as a file attachment
When applying for a service, benefit or job, you must follow the requirements for that application.
- File type: Some applications may ask you to provide your e-certificate in a specific format like jpg or png.
- Passport: If you apply for a new adult passport , you must print your e-certificate.
- Social insurance number (SIN):
- You can apply online for your SIN using your e-certificate.
- If you apply in person , you must print your e-certificate. You can get your SIN the same day.

context.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
context.text:
Other citizenship applications
This includes applications
- for a minor 13 and under to become a Canadian citizen
- for a citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship)
- to resume Canadian citizenship after giving it up
Send us a web form and include the following:
- a detailed description of the issue
- your e-certificate number
If your organization receives e-certificates
Your organization may receive e-certificates from your applicants if they
- apply for a service, benefit or job with your organization
- must prove their Canadian citizenship as part of the application
Regardless of the format, the e-certificate from your applicant is valid proof of their Canadian citizenship .

context.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
context.text:
Online application for a citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship)
In most cases, you’ll get the letter in your IRCC secure account .
- If you asked us to communicate with you through email after you applied, we’ll send the letter to the last email address you gave us .
- If you applied with the help of a representative, we’ll email them the letter .
If you applied with the help of a representative
Your representative will receive the letter with instructions on how to download your e-certificate.
To download your e-certificate without going through your representative, use this page to create your own IRCC Portal account .
You may still ask your representative to forward you the instructions letter.
- Do not use the invite code in the letter. You must request a new invitation code using your own email in the IRCC portal.
- The letter has other helpful information about your e-certificate, such as where in the IRCC Portal you can download the file.

context.title: Open work permits for family members of work permit holders: How to apply
context.text:
Proof that the principal applicant has included the family member in their application for permanent residence

context.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: After you apply
context.text:

You (the sponsor) can link their application for them if you’re managing your family members’ application and you’re designated as their representative.
See the top questions about linking your application .

context.title: Sponsor your relatives: How to apply
context.text:
- download, complete, and sign this form by hand along with your common-law partner, if this applies.

context.title: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: How to apply
context.text:
Who counts as your family member

If you want to sponsor a child through intercountry adoption, or if you want to sponsor an orphaned family member

- Permanent residence application: Your spouse, partner or child applies for permanent residence.
The principal applicant (the person you’re sponsoring) will submit both applications together online using the Permanent Residence (PR) Portal.
Apply through the PR Portal

context.title: Valid proofs of Canadian citizenship
context.text:
Electronic certificates (e-certificates)
The e-certificate is the digital format of the citizenship certificate. It’s a valid proof of Canadian citizenship that has
- a certificate number that starts with an "X"
- This is the only difference with a paper certificate (where the number starts with a "K" )
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
- your family name and given name(s)
- your date of birth
- your gender (male, female or another gender)
- the effective date of citizenship
Learn more about e-certificates , including how to
- download and print the e-certificate
- contact us if there are any issues

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: After you apply
context.text:
If you asked for an electronic certificate (e-certificate)
We’ll send the link to the e-certificate or your refusal letter to the email address you provided in your application.
If you asked for a paper certificate
If you’re a Canadian citizen, we’ll mail your certificate to your mailing address in Canada or the United States.
If you’re not a citizen, we’ll send your refusal letter to the email address you provided in your application.
If you applied on paper from Canada or the United States (no email provided)
After we check that your application is complete, you’ll get
- an acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter or email and
- your unique client identifier (UCI) (opens in a new tab)
If you have a tracking number with a postal or courier service, you can check if they delivered your application to us.

context.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
context.text:
If you fail the test and you applied as a family or group
When you apply as a family or group, we process all your applications together.
In some cases, we may be able to separate some applications. If you want to find out if you can separate your application to attend the ceremony on your own, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your invitation.

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: After you apply
context.text:
If you asked for an electronic certificate (e-certificate)
If you’re a Canadian citizen, we’ll send the link to the e-certificate to the email address provided in your application.
If you’re not a citizen, we’ll send your refusal letter to the email address provided in your application.
If you asked for a paper certificate
If you’re a Canadian citizen, we’ll mail your certificate to the embassy, high commission or consulate where you submitted your application.
If you’re not a citizen, we’ll send your refusal letter to the email address provided in your application.

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
context.text:
Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
- 1. About the process
- 2. Who can apply
- 3. How to apply
- 4. After you apply
Before you start, check if you can apply for a citizenship certificate .
Documents proving Canadian citizenship of your parent, grandparent and parental ancestor
Your application must be supported by authentic, reliable and verifiable documents for every generation in your application.
Your documents must
- be issued by the original authority that created or keeps the record
- This includes documents issued by a civil registry or a vital statistics office.
- clearly show who issued the document
Your application can’t be supported solely by third party records .
- If you find records like these, official documents likely exist. You should request them from the original authority.

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
context.text:
Stage 3: 14 days before the ceremony
With 2 weeks to go, it’s time to finalize the schedule and confirm all arrangements.
- Review the detailed sequence of events prepared by the clerk of the ceremony.
- Confirm any special arrangements for guest speakers, performances, music or entertainment, such as smudging ceremonies or security requirements.
- Review the host representative’s remarks with IRCC staff.
- Address any special requests from participants.
- Prepare a news release.
- Invite media outlets.
- Finalize the reception menu , considering dietary restrictions.
- Start media promotion, if applicable.
- Consider attending an in-person ceremony if you’re unfamiliar with how a ceremony unfolds.

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
context.text:
- Plan the layout of the venue: chairs, stage, podium, tables, green room, registration and reception area.
- Decide if a news release is needed.
- Plan the reception (optional).
- Recruit volunteers to serve as ushers and reception hosts (include bilingual volunteers).
- Share public transportation details with IRCC staff.
- Book a photographer, if needed.
- Book audiovisual setup (optional but recommended).
- Finalize catering and floral arrangements, if applicable.
- Organize a clean-up committee.
- Consider offering water to attendees using biodegradable containers (no plastic bottles or cups).
- Discuss ideas for small gifts (optional) to be given out at the receiving line, including cost and bilingual messaging.

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: When and where to host a ceremony
context.text:
Community venue checklist
Make sure the venue
- comfortably accommodates new citizens and guests
- This includes a stage that can accommodate a lectern or podium, a portrait of the monarch, a large Canadian flag and seating for the presiding official, clerk and special guests.
- This includes seats for candidates and their guests.
- is fully accessible, including the washrooms, ceremony platform and stage
- For example, it has accessible parking and wheelchair access to the ceremony venue and the stage.
- can accommodate a smudging , a cultural practice that may be requested by Indigenous participants
- Inform IRCC if a smudging can’t be done at the venue.
- has a separate dressing room for the presiding official and the clerk of the ceremony
- isn’t associated with alcohol sales or advertising, gambling, drugs or inappropriate behaviour
- has separate meeting rooms or areas for
- candidate registration upon arrival
- special guests (green room before and after the ceremony)

context.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Who can host a ceremony
context.text:
Who can host a ceremony
We encourage collaborations with a wide variety of groups and organizations to make citizenship ceremonies open and welcoming to the general public.
Your organization can work with us as the “host” of the ceremony.
Eligible hosts
Groups or organizations that can host a ceremony include:
- non-governmental and non-profit organizations
- educational institutions
- service organizations
- veterans’ organizations
- libraries
- volunteer groups
- various community groups
- government organizations or departments at all levels (federal, provincial/territorial, municipal)
- for example, City of Montréal, Province of Manitoba, provincial courts, Parks Canada

context.title: Minor children travelling to Canada
context.text:
The letter does not need to be certified. A photocopy of the parents’ or legal guardians’ signed passports or national identity cards should be attached to the letter.
Note: The border services officer may not ask to see these documents when the child enters Canada; however, it is strongly recommended that you bring them. The minor child will not be admitted to Canada if the officer is not convinced that the parents or legal guardians have authorized their stay.

context.title: Minor children travelling to Canada
context.text:
Minor children entering Canada as a visitor
The documents a minor child needs to enter Canada depend on whether the child is travelling alone or with someone.
If a minor child is travelling alone
The child should present
- their own passport
- A parent’s passport, even if the child’s details are included in it, cannot be used.
- a copy of their birth certificate, and
- a letter of authorization, in English or French if possible, which is signed by both parents or by their legal guardian and includes
- the parents’ (or legal guardian’s) address and telephone number, and
- the name, address and telephone number of the adult who will look after the child in Canada

context.title: Minor children travelling to Canada
context.text:
If a minor child is travelling with one parent only
The parent should present
- the child’s passport
- a copy of the child’s birth certificate, and
- a letter of authorization, in English or French if possible, which is signed by the parent who is not travelling with them and includes
- the address and telephone number of the parent who is not travelling, and
- a photocopy of that parent’s signed passport or national identity card
If the parents are separated or divorced and share custody of the child
- The parent travelling with the child should carry copies of the legal custody documents.
- It is also best to have a letter of authorization from the other parent who has custody to take the child on a trip out of the country.

question: Will the change to the first-generation limit to citizenship by descent affect those who became Canadian citizens before Bill C-3 became law?

context.title: Change to citizenship rules in 2025
context.text:
Change to citizenship rules in 2025
On December 15, 2025, the Government of Canada passed Bill C-3, An Act to amend the Citizenship Act . This legislation changes the first-generation limit to citizenship by descent.
On this page, we explain what this change means, how to check if you’re affected, and what you need to do before travelling to Canada.
This change officially took effect on December 15, 2025 .
What the change means
Before Bill C-3, Canadian citizenship by descent was limited to the first generation born outside Canada. This rule was called the first-generation limit to citizenship. The changes made by Bill C-3 removed this limit in some situations.
This change to the first-generation limit doesn’t affect anyone who already became a Canadian citizen before Bill C-3 became law. If you were already a citizen before the bill, you’re still a citizen.

context.title: Canadian citizenship

Canadian citizenship
Apply to become a Canadian citizen, study for the test or get proof of citizenship.
Status of changes to the first-generation limit on citizenship by descent Updated December 15, 2025
On December 15, 2025, the Government of Canada passed Bill C-3 to change the first-generation limit on citizenship by descent.
The Ontario Superior Court of Justice ruled in December 2023 that the limit was unconstitutional for many people. In March 2025, we introduced an interim measure to support those affected.
We will now process all applications submitted under the interim measure using the new rules.
Learn more about this change .

context.title: International Experience Canada: Who can apply - Eligibility by country and category
context.text:
Changes to program participation for Italian citizens
As of November 1, 2022, Italian citizens can participate in the International Experience Canada program twice. Under the previous agreement, Italian citizens could only participate once.
If you submitted an application under the previous agreement
If you submitted your application before November 1, 2022, you can apply to participate a second time in the category of your choice. You can only participate in the IEC program twice.
Description: The Working Holiday category is designed for Italian citizens who wish to find temporary paid employment (for up to 12 months) to pay for their travel in Canada.
Note: As an Italian citizen, you may participate in IEC twice under any category.
To be eligible for the Working Holiday category, you must
- be an Italian citizen
- have a valid Italian passport for the duration of your stay in Canada
- Your work permit in Canada can’t be valid longer than your passport.

context.text:

- completed your study program
- applied for permanent residence

context.title: Dual Canadian citizens need a valid Canadian passport
context.text:
Find out if you are eligible for a special authorization to board your flight to Canada
You can apply for a special authorization if you:
- have not been issued a Canadian passport that is valid on the day of your travel
- have a flight to Canada that leaves in less than 10 days
- have a valid passport from a visa-exempt country or territory
- are not a Canadian-American dual citizen
And one of the following:
- have previously received a certificate of Canadian citizenship, or
- held a Canadian passport in the past, or
- were granted Canadian citizenship after having been a permanent resident of Canada.
Your information will be verified in our electronic systems to confirm that you are a Canadian citizen. This authorization will be valid for only 4 days from the date of travel you select on the form . If you don’t use it within this time, you will need to apply for a new authorization.

- be an Italian citizen

question: How do I start the citizenship test after receiving an invitation?

context.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
context.text:
Wait for a test invitation
You need an invitation to take the test online.
What’s on the invitation
We’ll send you an invitation by email to take the online test after you submit your citizenship application. The test invitation is a PDF attachment in an email. The PDF includes instructions on what to do before, during and after the test.
Your invitation should have
- a test start date and end date (you’ll have 30 days to take it)
- a link to the test (or directions for an in-person test)
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
- an email address you can use to contact us

context.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
context.text:
You must wait until you receive your invitation before you can take the test. You can’t book the test yourself or contact us to get an invitation. We’ll send the invitation as quickly as possible.
You can check your application status to confirm that your invitation is on its way. When you check, go to the “Citizenship test” section of the status tracker. The In progress status means that
- we have scheduled your test
- you’ll get your invitation soon
Check your application status

context.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
context.text:
When you can take the test
If you take the test online , you can take your test only between the start date and end date provided on your invitation. This will be a 30-day period.
After you receive your invitation, you
- have up to 3 chances to pass the test during the 30-day period
- If you fail, log in and try again to use your chances.
- can take the test at any time during the 30-day period (including weekends and holidays)
You can’t sign in to the test
- before or after the 30-day period on your invitation or
- after you submit the test

context.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
context.text:
How you’ll get the invitation
If you gave an email address in your application, we’ll send you or your representative the invitation by email .
To avoid missing our emails
- check your junk or spam folder
- look for an invitation from an email address that ends in “@cic.gc.ca” or “@canada.ca”
If you or your representative did not give an email address in your application you can provide your email using our web form . If you don’t provide an email
- we’ll mail the invitation to you or
- we may call you (check your voicemail messages regularly)

context.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
context.text:
How to start the test
- Sign in
- Sign in to the online test only after you receive an invitation.
- Use your application number and your unique client identifier (UCI) to sign in.
- Read and accept the privacy notice, and the terms and conditions.
- Request the test link and check your email
- Select the “Email me the test link” button at the bottom of the page. We’ll send the link to the same email address that received the test invitation (the email on your citizenship application) or your representative’s email.
- If you’re using a representative, you’ll have an option to send the link to your email instead of theirs.
- It may take a few minutes for you or your representative to receive the test link.
- The link expires after 15 minutes. If your link expires, sign in again to get a new test link.
- If you sent yourself a test link multiple times, use the latest test link to sign in.
- Confirm your identity
- Re-enter your application number and UCI to confirm your identity.

context.title: International Experience Canada: Create your IEC profile and get your invitation to apply
context.text:
Step 1: Use the IRCC secure account to check your eligibility
Create or sign in to your account and select “International Experience Canada” to start the questionnaire and check your eligibility. Your answers will be saved automatically to help complete your profile.
The questionnaire takes 10 minutes to complete. You’ll be asked about your
- country of citizenship
- country of permanent residence (where you live permanently)
- This is the country where you have a permanent address. For example, if you’re a Mexican student in Canada, your country of permanent residence is Mexico.
- country of residence (where you live now)
- student status (if this applies to you)
- job offer (if this applies to you)
- confirmation letter from an IEC recognized organization (if this applies to you)
- Recognized organizations are different from representatives , who can help with your immigration or citizenship application.
Create or sign in to your IRCC secure account

context.title: Study permit: Get the right documents
context.text:
Show proof of identity Always required
To show proof of identity, you (and each family member who comes with you) must have
- a copy of a valid passport or travel document
- Upload a copy of the information page of your passport when you apply online.
- If you’re approved , you must send us your original passport.
- 2 recent passport size photos
- The name and date of birth of the person must be written on the back of each photo.
For citizens or lawful permanent residents of the United States (U.S.)
If you’re a citizen of the U.S., you have options for what you can show as proof of identity .
If you’re a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., you must travel with a valid green card ( or equivalent official proof of status in the U.S. ) and a valid passport from their country of nationality (or an equivalent document).

context.title: International Experience Canada: About the program
context.text:
An image shows a generic example of a police certificate.
Make sure you get the right police certificate. Check our website for specific instructions.
Text displays: “Accept your invitation to apply (ITA)”
An image shows a generic example of an invitation to apply letter. A calendar page displays the number 10 beside a thumbs-up and a thumbs-down.
If you get an invitation to apply, you will have 10 days to accept or decline. Remember, all of your deadlines will be in UTC time.
The text “UTC time” on the letter is highlighted and expanded. Pages fall off the calendar as it counts down. A cursor hesitates between thumbs-up and thumbs-down.
Not ready to accept the invitation? You can decline the invitation, go back into the pool and be eligible for another invitation.
But if time runs out on your invitation, your name will be removed from the pool.
Text displays: “Complete your work permit application”
Text displays: “Do not wait until the last day to submit your application”

context.title: Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot : After you apply
context.text:
If we approve your application
We’ll send you
- a port of entry letter of introduction
- This isn’t your study permit.
- You need to show this letter to the officer when you arrive in Canada.
- an electronic travel authorization (eTA) or a visitor (temporary resident) visa, depending on which you need to enter Canada
If you need an eTA
Your letter of introduction will have information about it. Your eTA will be electronically linked to your passport and will be valid for 5 years or until your passport expires, whichever comes first. Make sure you travel with the passport you used to apply.

context.title: Study permit: How to apply
context.text:
6. We check your identity when you arrive in Canada
When you arrive, we check your identity to make sure that you are the same person who was approved to travel to Canada. We may use your biometrics to do this.
If we can’t verify your identity, you may be detained by a border services officer. These officers help protect the health and safety of Canadians.
If the officer determines that you’re not admissible to Canada, you won’t be allowed to enter Canada. If you came by air, you’ll have to take a return flight to where you came from.

context.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Wait for a decision
context.text:
If you don’t want to become a Canadian citizen anymore
Find out how to withdraw or cancel your application .
Quality Assurance Program
Our Quality Assurance Program randomly selects applications for a detailed review. If your application is selected, we’ll
- let you know by email or mail
- ask you to provide additional information
- schedule an interview with our official, which will help us to
- confirm the accuracy of the documents and information you provided
- make sure you filled out your application correctly
- verify that you meet all the citizenship requirements
Print all pages in this section

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: After you apply
context.text:
Receiving your certificate or refusal letter
We’ll mail your paper certificate or refusal letter to the embassy, high commission or consulate where you submitted your application.
Quality assurance program
Our quality assurance program randomly chooses applications for review. If yours is chosen, we’ll ask you to attend an interview where we’ll
- review and verify the original documents you submitted
- verify that the information you provided on your application form is accurate
- request additional supporting documents, up to and including DNA to confirm parentage, if we’re not satisfied with the documents on file
Note: We’ll notify you in writing if your application is chosen for an interview.

context.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Wait for a decision
context.text:
Wait for a decision
Learn what happens after you submit your application and how you can track its status.
What happens first
When the Case Processing Centre in Sydney (CPC Sydney) receives your application, the staff there will check that you
- included all the required documents
- paid the correct fees
If your application is complete , we’ll start processing your application and send you an acknowledgement of receipt letter.
If your application is incomplete or missing fees, we’ll return your application to you.
After the initial review, CPC Sydney sends your application to a local IRCC office to make a final decision. You may be asked to attend an interview with a citizenship officer or a citizenship judge.

context.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: After you apply
context.text:
If we approve your application
- we’ll invite you to take the oath of citizenship at the citizenship ceremony
- you’ll receive a Canadian citizenship certificate
You may withdraw your application . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund .

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: After you apply
context.text:
If you applied on paper from Canada or the United States (email provided)
After we check that your application is complete, you’ll get
- an acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter or email and
- your unique client identifier (UCI) (opens in a new tab)
If you have a tracking number with a postal or courier service, you can check if they delivered your application to us.
Incomplete paper application
If your application is incomplete, we’ll
- return your application and
- send you a letter asking you to resubmit the application with the missing information

context.title: International Experience Canada: About the program
context.text:
Applying for International Experience Canada?
Before you apply, visit our website to find out if your country is part of the program and, if so, which of the 3 categories are available to you.
Text displays: “Check out the application process at a glance”
A 1-page overview of the application process is shown.
Check out our application process at a glance for an overview of all the steps to apply.
Text displays: “Create and submit your International Experience Canada (IEC) profile”
An applicant creates an account.
After completing the Come to Canada questionnaire, create and submit your profile and choose the pools that apply to you.
An applicant uploads documents to the program website.
While you wait for an invitation to apply, start preparing your supporting documents. This may take a while, so it’s better to start early.
An image shows a generic example of a police certificate.
Make sure you get the right police certificate. Check our website for specific instructions.

context.title: International Experience Canada: After you apply
context.text:
- proof of an appointment for your medical examination, or
- a receipt for your police certificate request.
Your application won’t be complete if we only receive your proof of an appointment for a medical examination or a receipt for your police certificate request.
We’ll contact you if we need additional documents. You must submit the requested documents before the deadline we give in the request letter.
Requests for additional documents can affect processing times.
Learn more about
- how to submit a document we requested
- what to do if you can’t submit a document we requested
Wait until your application is approved before you
- buy a plane ticket for any travel to Canada
- buy health insurance for your stay in Canada
- make commitments to your prospective employer in Canada
- commit to any accommodation in Canada
- cancel your accommodation or leave your job or studies in your home country

context.title: International Experience Canada: Create your IEC profile and get your invitation to apply
context.text:
Step 1: Use the IRCC secure account to check your eligibility
Create or sign in to your account and select “International Experience Canada” to start the questionnaire and check your eligibility. Your answers will be saved automatically to help complete your profile.
The questionnaire takes 10 minutes to complete. You’ll be asked about your
- country of citizenship
- country of permanent residence (where you live permanently)
- This is the country where you have a permanent address. For example, if you’re a Mexican student in Canada, your country of permanent residence is Mexico.
- country of residence (where you live now)
- student status (if this applies to you)
- job offer (if this applies to you)
- confirmation letter from an IEC recognized organization (if this applies to you)
- Recognized organizations are different from representatives , who can help with your immigration or citizenship application.
Create or sign in to your IRCC secure account

context.title: International Experience Canada: Who can apply - Eligibility by country and category
context.text:
If you submitted an application under the previous agreement
If you submitted your application before November 1, 2022, you can apply to participate a second time in the category of your choice. You can only participate in the IEC program twice.
Description: The Young Professionals category is designed for Italian citizens, including recent post-secondary graduates, who wish to further their careers by gaining professional work experience in Canada. Participants must have a signed letter of offer or a signed contract of employment (for up to 12 months) before submitting their profile to the pool.
Note: As an Italian citizen, you may participate in IEC twice under any category.
To be eligible for the Young Professionals category, you must
- be an Italian citizen
- have a valid Italian passport for the duration of your stay in Canada
- Your work permit in Canada can’t be valid longer than your passport.
- prove you’re a resident of Italy when you apply

context.title: Express Entry: After you apply
context.text:
Decision on your application
The decision we make on your application will be based on if you:
- are eligible for the program
- are admissible to Canada, based on the results of your:
- medical exam
- police certificates
- background checks
When we make a decision on your application, we’ll let you know through your IRCC secure account .
If we approve your application
- Make sure to pay your right of permanent residence fee if you haven’t already done so. We can’t approve your application until you’ve paid all fees.
- Find out what to do next .
If we reject or refuse your application
To be considered in future rounds of invitations, you have to:
- fill out and submit a new Express Entry profile
- meet the eligibility criteria
- be accepted into the pool again

context.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: How to apply
context.text:
First-time applicants
If this is the first time you have applied for citizenship, you will need to send the original or a clear and easily readable certified copy of the required documents.
If those documents are not in English or French, you must provide the original documents or clear and easily readable certified copies, a translation of them, and an affidavit from the person who did the translation. Translations by family members are not acceptable.
Previous applicants
If you have applied for citizenship in the past, you may provide photocopies of the required documents.

context.title: Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship: After you apply
context.text:
Some applications may take longer to process
- If documents or fees (if applicable) are missing, we will return your application to you.
- If your case is complex, we may contact you to ask for more information or documents. Such cases may take longer to process.
Check the status of your application online . If the normal processing times have passed and you cannot check the status of your application online, you can send us an enquiry by using this Web form .
A citizenship officer may need to interview you
If so, we’ll notify you by mail of the time and place of your interview.
- If you live outside Canada, the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate responsible for your area will contact you to let you know how the interview will be conducted.
- If you need to change your appointment, contact the office that sent you the invitation.
- The contact information is in the letter we sent you.
You may withdraw your application . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund .

context.title: How to withdraw or cancel a citizenship application
context.text:
How to withdraw or cancel a citizenship application
To withdraw or cancel a citizenship application you’ve already submitted, you must
- prepare your documents
- send your request using the correct method
In some cases, you may be able to get a refund for some or all of your fees. Find out if you can ask for a refund .
1. Prepare your documents
To withdraw your application
- complete and sign the Request for Withdrawal of Citizenship Application Form (CIT 0027) (opens in new tab)
- If you applied as a family or a group, each applicant must fill out and sign the form (1 form per applicant, including minors if applicable).
- get a copy of your fee receipt

context.title: How to withdraw or cancel a citizenship application
context.text:
Giving up Canadian citizenship (from outside Canada or the United States): Use the web form or send your documents by mail
You can send your documents to us through the web form or by mail.
Option 1 (recommended): Web form
You need to
- send your documents through the web form (opens in a new tab) and
- inform the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate (opens in a new tab) where you submitted your application that you sent a withdrawal request
Option 2: By mail
You can mail your request to the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate (opens in a new tab) where you submitted your application.

context.title: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: After you apply
context.text:
Keep your information up to date
Update your contact information or tell us about changes to your family situation, for example, marriage, birth, divorce or death.
Withdraw your sponsorship application
You can request to withdraw your sponsorship application any time before the people you’re sponsoring become permanent residents.
You may be able to get a refund if we haven’t started processing your application.
How to request to withdraw your sponsorship application
Use our web form to request to withdraw your sponsorship application.
In your request, include your
- full name
- date of birth
- country of birth
- application number, if you know it
- unique client identifier ( UCI ), if you know it
- signed withdrawal request letter
Once we receive your request, we’ll review it and confirm if your application has been withdrawn.
If the people you’re sponsoring become permanent residents before we process your request, you’re responsible for them for the undertaking period .

context.title: Express Entry: After you apply
context.text:
If your personal information changes
To avoid processing delays, use the web form to tell us about changes to your personal information as soon as possible.
Go to web form
You must let us know if:
- you want to withdraw your application
- your family composition changes, such as:
- birth or adoption of a child
- marriage or divorce
- you change your immigration representative
- your contact information (mailing address, email address, telephone number) changes
- a province or territory withdraws your nomination
- you don’t plan to live in the province or territory nominating you
- your job or job offer changes
- you get a new educational credential
- you get updated language test results

context.title: Sponsor your relatives: After you apply
context.text:
Withdraw your sponsorship application
You can withdraw your sponsorship application any time before the relative you’re sponsoring becomes a permanent resident of Canada.
You may be able to get a refund if we haven’t started processing your application.
Use our web form to request the withdrawal of your sponsorship application. In your request, include your
- full name
- date of birth
- country of birth
- application number (if you know it)
- relative’s client ID number (UCI) (if you know it)
- signed withdrawal request letter

context.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: After you apply
context.text:
If your processing time has passed
If the normal processing time for your application has passed, you can contact us using our web form .
Withdraw your sponsorship application
You can request to withdraw your sponsorship application any time before the person you’re sponsoring becomes a permanent resident of Canada.
You may be able to get a refund if we haven’t started processing your application.
Use our web form to request the withdrawal of your sponsorship application.
In your request, include your
- full name
- date of birth
- country of birth
- application number (if you know it)
- UCI (if you know it)
- signed withdrawal request letter

context.title: Study permit: How to apply
context.text:
Apply online
If you’re applying for a study permit, you must apply online , whether you’re outside of Canada or already in Canada.
You’re only eligible to apply on paper if you
- have a disability that prevents you from applying online
- hold an identity or travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons
Get faster processing as a doctoral student New
If you’re a doctoral (PhD) student, you and your accompanying family members may be able to get faster processing on your applications.
Check if you’re eligible and learn how to get your applications processed faster.

context.title: Search of citizenship records: How to apply
context.text:
Start your online application
In the account
- we’ll check if you can apply online
- you can apply online urgently if you qualify
Once you start your online application, you have 60 days to submit it.
The online application works best in Google Chrome.
Create an account or sign in
Apply on paper for your or someone else’s records
If you’ve already applied online, do not apply on paper for the same request. If you do, we won’t process your paper application.
Get the application package
The application package has the instruction guide and the form you must fill out.
- Read the instruction guide carefully before you complete the form.
- If information or documents are missing , it may delay the processing of your application.

context.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: After you apply
context.text:
Withdrawing your application
You may withdraw (cancel) your application (opens in a new tab) . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund (opens in a new tab) .
Final decision
If you are a Canadian citizen and we approve your application, you’ll get a citizenship certificate.
- If there’s a mistake on the certificate, find out how to fix it (opens in a new tab) .
- Find out when to contact us (opens in a new tab) if we informed you that we’ve mailed your certificate, but you still haven’t received it.
If you’re not a Canadian citizen, we’ll send you a refusal letter. Your fee will not be refunded.

context.title: Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship: After you apply
context.text:
Some applications may take longer to process
- If documents or fees (if applicable) are missing, we will return your application to you.
- If your case is complex, we may contact you to ask for more information or documents. Such cases may take longer to process.
Check the status of your application online . If the normal processing times have passed and you cannot check the status of your application online, you can send us an enquiry by using this Web form .
A citizenship officer may need to interview you
If so, we’ll notify you by mail of the time and place of your interview.
- If you live outside Canada, the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate responsible for your area will contact you to let you know how the interview will be conducted.
- If you need to change your appointment, contact the office that sent you the invitation.
- The contact information is in the letter we sent you.
You may withdraw your application . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund .

context.title: Search of citizenship records: How to apply
context.text:
How to get a paper copy of your result
We send the result of your search electronically to the email address in your application form.
If you need a paper copy of the result
- let us know in the application form
- you may need to wait longer due to delivery times
- you will not receive the electronic letter
Pay the application fee
You can pay your fees online.
- Methods of payment depend on where you’re applying from.
- If you’re submitting more than 1 application at the same time, you can pay all the fees together.
- You cannot get a refund once we start processing your application.
- If you need help, check the payment instructions .
Pay your fees online (opens in a new tab)

context.title: Search of citizenship records: How to apply
context.text:
Search of citizenship records: How to apply
- 1. About the process
- 2. How to apply
- 3. After you apply
Before you apply, make sure you’re eligible for a search of citizenship records.
Apply online to get your own records
You can apply online only to get your own records . To get someone else’s record , you need to apply on paper .
If you’ve already applied on paper, do not apply online for the same request. If you do, we won’t process your online application.
If you need to apply online urgently
We can process applications faster than our normal processing times in special cases , such as
- confirming to a foreign government that you’re not a citizen (for example, to get a passport from that country)
- administering the estate of a deceased person or executing a will
- showing you are (or are not) a citizen to get a certain job

question: What should I do if I see a blank screen or a message that my browser isn’t supported when taking the citizenship test?

context.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
context.text:
Blank screen or message that browser isn’t supported
If you see a blank screen or a message that your browser isn’t supported, make sure you’re using Chrome or Safari .
If you’re already using Chrome or Safari, try
- updating your Chrome or Safari to the latest version
- disabling your browser extensions
- clearing your browser’s cookies and cache
- turning off hardware acceleration and restarting the browser (if you use Chrome)
- restarting your browser or device
- reinstalling your browser and keeping all the default settings
- using a different device to take the test
If you still have issues signing in, email the address in your test invitation.

context.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
context.text:
Get your identification (ID)
Get a piece of ID, for example
- your permanent resident card (even if it’s expired) or
- a valid (not expired) piece of ID with your photo and signature on it (for example, a driver’s licence or health card)
Use the right devices and browsers
You must take the test
- on a desktop computer, laptop or tablet with a webcam
- using a Chrome or Safari Web browser
Do not take the test
- on a mobile phone
- using Chrome on an iPad
- on a Microsoft Surface Pro
- on a virtual private network (VPN)

context.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
context.text:
Webcam can’t connect to the online test system
If your webcam isn’t working and can’t connect to the online test system, find help related to using
- the Chrome browser
- You can’t take the test with Chrome on an iPad at this time.
- the Chrome operating system (OS) and Chromebook
- the Mac OS and Safari browser
- Windows 7
- Windows 8
- Windows 10
- Windows 11
- a tablet
Fixing webcam issues in a tablet
Option 1
- Close all other applications and web pages that you won’t use for the test.
- Click “ ok ” if you see an error message on the test web page or refresh the page.
- Sign in to the test again (opens in a new tab)
Option 2
- Reset or restart your tablet.
- Sign in to the test again (opens in a new tab)
If your webcam is working , but it can’t connect to the online test system, you may see this error message:
Follow these steps:
- Try using a different device to take the test.

context.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
context.text:
What to do and not to do during the test
To avoid having to retake the test for a technical reason, make sure you
- turn on your webcam and check that your face is fully visible in the frame
- have a reliable Internet connection
- have no other tabs, windows or programs open on the computer
- turn off your virtual private network (VPN)
- give yourself enough time to take the test (because the timer can’t be paused)
For your test to be valid, you must
- take the test alone
- take the test in the same place you took the photo of yourself and your ID before the test
- make sure there are no items in the background that have your personal information on them (like a diploma)
There are also some things you must not do during the test:
- Don’t use any other devices.
- Don’t look at any study materials.
- Don’t use the back button in your web browser.

context.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
context.text:
If you cannot take the test online
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you
- have a weak or unreliable Internet connection
- have no access to an electronic device or webcam
- cannot use the supported browsers for the test (Chrome or Safari)
Face covering (online test)
Your face must be fully visible through your webcam during the online test.
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you can’t remove your face covering.
Ceremony accommodations
We may invite you to a virtual or an in-person ceremony.
